title: GPU nodepool lifecycle abstraction and rollout module for Private VPC (ASG + Karpenter)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: build a composable Terraform module to manage GPU node pools in customer Private VPCs that supports both ASG-based and Karpenter-backed scaling strategies, safe OS/driver upgrades, and production health checks. The module should provide a single lifecycle abstraction so platform teams can consistently perform rollouts (canary, blue/green, and rolling with cordon/drain), enforce GPU driver consistency, and integrate with our observability hooks (Console tracing + alerts).

Scope:
- Provision node pool resources and IAM roles for both ASG and Karpenter provisioners inside customer VPCs.
- Expose a simple interface: node_pool_name, gpu_profile, instance_mix, min/max/target, taints/labels, upgrade_strategy, drain_timeout, health_probe_config, and driver_installation_strategy.
- Implement safe upgrade strategies: (A) in-place rolling upgrade with cordon/drain and GPU driver pre-warm; (B) create-new-pool + add-to-load (blue/green) then decommission old pool.
- Health hooks: per-node health check using a TCP/HTTP probe against a node-exporter endpoint, kubelet readiness, and a post-drain validation test that verifies KV cache persistence for serving nodes. Hooks integrate with existing ops-runbook links and can trigger automated rollback via a recorded metric threshold.
- Provide helper Terraform resources and null_resource local-exec hooks for driver/OS reconciler where the cloud provider/AMI changes require graceful node replacement.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We model the module as 'declarative desired state' but use lightweight null_resource hooks for steps that cannot be expressed purely in HCL (ex: triggering Karpenter provisioning drain sequences). This avoids heavy custom controllers while keeping Terraform as the single source of truth for infra drift.
- To handle mixed spot/on-demand fleets, the module exposes ordered instance_pools. The orchestration for blue/green will prefer on-demand to stabilize canaries, then fill with spot capacity. This adds complexity to the module but greatly reduces customer-visible regression risk during upgrades.
- We opted not to implement a full controller inside the module (no long-running manager) to keep the private stack air-gapped friendly. Instead we rely on operators (kubectl/CI runners) invoked from the customer's control plane or our support automation.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Module deploys identical node pools for an internal E2E test VPC (ASG and Karpenter modes) without manual steps.
2) Upgrade strategy B (create-new-pool + swap) completes for a 200-node cluster with <2% serving error rate and controlled latency impact (observability dashboards show regression <5%).
3) Health hooks detect a simulated bad driver image and auto-fail the rollout, with an automated rollback plan executed by an ops-runbook (documented).
4) Module passes terraform fmt/lint, unit tests (terragrunt plan comparisons), and a CI validate stage that runs the null_resource hooks in a dry-run mode.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: autoscaling policy ML inference-aware batching parameters, full on-prem bare-metal driver installers, and UI changes in Console. Those will be follow-ups if this module proves stable.

Implementation notes:
- Main entrypoint is a single module root that delegates to submodules for asg_provisioner and karpenter_provisioner. Submodules are simple and isolated so teams can import only what they need.
- Variables include: gpu_profile (g4dn/p4d), node_labels, node_taints, instance_types (ordered list), tenancy (spot|on-demand|mixed), driver_version, kubelet_version, max_unavailable, drain_grace_period, health_probe (path/port/retry), and canary_percentage.
- Outputs: current_nodepool_id, rollout_status_url (link to running runbook/CI job), last_successful_driver_version.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/GPU+Nodepool+Lifecycle+Module
- Draft module registry page: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/terraform-modules/gpu-nodepool
- Implementation branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/feat/gpu-nodepool-lifecycle
- Active PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/6421

Testing plan:
- Unit: terraform validate/plan diffs for all supported cloud providers.
- Integration: deploy into an isolated staging VPC using the internal test harness (mixed spot/on-demand, 3 node pools). Validate canary upgrade path, drain hooks, and rollback.
- Chaos: simulate instance terminations during rollout and ensure autoscaler fallback and healthprobe recover and do not leave unschedulable pods.

Next steps and blockers:
- Blocker: confirm KMS key access patterns for node bootstrap artifacts in air-gapped customers (security follow-up).
- Blocker: finalize driver packaging strategy with Research (packaged deb vs containerized driver installer).
- Next: land PR #6421 which contains the initial module scaffolding and unit tests, then run an internal staging run next week.
